prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed is a vehicle control device which is applied to a vehicle equipped with an engine (10) and an engine torque adjustment mechanism for adjusting an engine torque. The control device comprises a PCM (50) configured, upon satisfaction of a condition that the vehicle is traveling and a steering angle-related value relevant to a steering angle of a steering device is increasing, to control the engine torque adjustment mechanism to reduce the engine torque, so as to execute a vehicle attitude control for generating vehicle deceleration. The PCM (50) is configured, upon satisfaction of a vehicle attitude control-terminating condition for terminating the vehicle attitude control, to control the engine torque adjustment mechanism to restore the engine torque to an original level of torque before the execution of the vehicle attitude control. The PCM (50) is further configured to gradually ease the vehicle attitude control-terminating condition, as the number of times of combustion per unit time in the engine (10) becomes smaller.

outputs.L1: Disclosed is a vehicle control device for a vehicle equipped with an engine (10) and an engine torque adjustment mechanism configured to adjust engine torque. The control device comprises a PCM (50) configured, when the vehicle is traveling and a steering angle-related value associated with a steering angle of a steering device is increasing, to control the engine torque adjustment mechanism to reduce the engine torque, thereby executing vehicle attitude control that generates vehicle deceleration. Upon satisfaction of a vehicle attitude control termination condition, the PCM (50) controls the engine torque adjustment mechanism to restore the engine torque to its original level before execution of the vehicle attitude control. The PCM (50) is further configured to gradually relax the vehicle attitude control termination condition as the number of combustion events per unit time in the engine (10) decreases.
outputs.L2: A vehicle control apparatus is provided for use in a vehicle having an engine (10) and an engine-torque regulating mechanism. The apparatus includes a PCM (50) that performs vehicle attitude control by commanding the torque regulating mechanism to decrease engine torque and thereby decelerate the vehicle when the vehicle is moving and a parameter associated with the steering angle of a steering device is increasing. When a condition for ending the vehicle attitude control is met, the PCM (50) directs the torque regulating mechanism to return the engine torque to the level that existed before the attitude control began. In addition, the PCM (50) progressively relaxes the termination condition as the number of combustion events occurring per unit time in the engine (10) decreases.
outputs.L3:
The vehicle control device is intended for a vehicle equipped with an engine and an engine torque adjustment mechanism. While the vehicle is traveling, a powertrain control module (PCM) monitors a value related to the steering angle. When this value increases, the PCM reduces the engine torque, thereby decelerating the vehicle and stabilizing its attitude.

The PCM continues this vehicle attitude control until a specified termination condition is satisfied. Once the condition is met, the PCM ends the control operation and restores the engine torque to the level that existed before the vehicle attitude control began. To ensure smooth and appropriate control under different engine operating conditions, the PCM gradually relaxes the termination condition as the number of engine combustion events per unit time decreases.
outputs.L4:
A vehicle control device controls the attitude of a traveling vehicle by temporarily reducing engine torque in response to a steering operation. When a steering-related value, such as a steering angle, steering speed, or another value indicative of increased steering input, rises to a predetermined level, the device commands the engine to reduce the torque transmitted to the drive wheels. The resulting deceleration changes the load acting on the vehicle and helps suppress undesirable body motion, thereby improving stability and responsiveness during cornering.

After the torque reduction has begun, the device determines whether a prescribed termination condition has been satisfied. When that condition is met, the torque-reduction control is ended and the engine torque is restored, preferably in a controlled manner that avoids an abrupt change in vehicle behavior.

The timing of torque recovery is adjusted according to the operating state of the engine. In particular, the device obtains or estimates an engine combustion frequency and progressively relaxes the termination condition as that frequency decreases. Thus, at lower combustion frequencies, the system permits the reduced-torque state to be terminated under less restrictive conditions. This prevents torque recovery from being unnecessarily delayed when individual combustion events occur less frequently and engine response is correspondingly slower or more variable.

By coordinating the termination of vehicle attitude control with engine combustion frequency, the device can recover engine torque at an appropriate time across a wide range of engine speeds and operating conditions. The control therefore provides smoother acceleration recovery, reduces the likelihood of torque fluctuations or delayed response, and maintains stable, predictable vehicle behavior during and after steering maneuvers.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a vehicle control device that reduces engine torque during increasing steering input and restores torque when a termination condition is met, with the termination condition relaxed as engine combustion frequency decreases.
counterfactuals.output: A vehicle control device includes a controller configured to reduce torque generated by an engine when a steering input to the vehicle is increasing. The controller restores the engine torque when a termination condition for terminating the torque reduction is satisfied. The controller further changes the termination condition according to a combustion frequency of the engine such that the termination condition is relaxed as the combustion frequency decreases. Accordingly, torque reduction associated with increasing steering input can be terminated more readily during low-frequency engine combustion, thereby suppressing excessive or prolonged torque reduction while maintaining vehicle stability and steering responsiveness.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract describing a PCM-based vehicle attitude control system that generates deceleration by reducing engine torque while steering and gradually eases the control-termination condition at lower engine combustion rates.
counterfactuals.output: A vehicle attitude control system includes a powertrain control module (PCM) configured to generate vehicle deceleration by reducing engine torque when a prescribed steering condition is detected. The PCM determines whether to terminate the torque-reduction control based on an engine operating condition associated with combustion rate. As the engine combustion rate decreases, the PCM gradually relaxes the control-termination condition, thereby progressively permitting termination of the deceleration control. This approach maintains stable vehicle attitude during steering while avoiding abrupt torque recovery and improving drivability at low engine speeds or low combustion frequencies.

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a concise technical disclosure of a vehicle control apparatus equipped with an engine torque adjustment mechanism, including the conditions for initiating and terminating steering-related vehicle attitude control.
counterfactuals.output:
A vehicle control apparatus includes an engine, an electronically controlled engine-torque adjustment mechanism, a steering-state sensor, a vehicle-speed sensor, and a controller. The controller performs steering-related attitude control by temporarily reducing commanded engine torque to generate vehicle deceleration and increase front-wheel vertical load, thereby improving turn-in response.

The control is initiated when the vehicle is traveling above a prescribed speed and a detected steering parameter—such as steering-wheel angular velocity, steering-angle increase rate, or a calculated target lateral acceleration—exceeds an initiation threshold, indicating entry into a turn. Torque reduction is determined according to the steering parameter and may be limited based on accelerator demand, gear state, road conditions, and available engine torque.

The attitude control is terminated when the steering parameter falls below a lower termination threshold for a predetermined time, the steering angle begins returning toward neutral, the calculated lateral-acceleration demand ceases to increase, or an overriding condition occurs, such as braking, traction/stability-control intervention, low vehicle speed, or excessive torque limitation. At termination, the torque correction is ramped toward zero, and engine torque is smoothly restored to the driver-requested value to avoid driveline shock.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
